A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–B. Content can be matched across the revisions and page reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 training, MNIST and synthetic teacher-student experiments, ViT representation analyses, and sharpness experiments in Figures 1–14 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results, including training outcomes, representation-alignment measurements, and edge-of-stability experiments.

M1.justification: The studied models, training procedures, and first-order entropic loss in Eq. (3) remain unchanged. The revised treatment of weight decay concerns the mathematical derivation, without documenting a changed algorithm or training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, MNIST, ImageNet, and the same synthetic teacher-student and regression tasks. The expanded explanation of transformed datasets in Section 5.1 describes coverage already present in v1.

E2.justification: The SGD/Adam comparisons in Figures 10 and 12, input-alignment reference in Figure 3, and within-model and cross-model ViT comparisons are retained. The corrected ViT axis labels clarify comparisons already described in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains the same architectures, optimizers, learning rates, budgets, batch sizes, and metrics, including 300 ImageNet images for ViT CKA. Figure 5's caption correction agrees with the stability threshold already used in v1 and does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The batch-size and weight-decay analyses, gradient-balance trajectories, entropy correlations, and noise-balance sharpness tests are retained. The added width-bottleneck calculation is a theoretical extension, without a corresponding new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Five-run averaging in Figures 7 and 9 and the existing shaded plots are retained. No new run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, or statistical tests are disclosed.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 13 update the displayed ViT alignment values under the same stated evaluation setup, while preserving the broad alignment patterns. Other experimental results, including ResNet18's 98% training and 88% test accuracy, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 introduces the regularized loss into Theorem 1 and qualifies Eq. (3) as first order in both learning rate and weight decay. Appendix B.11 adds a limited extension deriving partial alignment when one network is narrower than the target rank, culminating in Eq. (74); the existing main theorem suite is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about symmetry breaking, gradient balance, universal representations, and sharpness. Naming Theorem 8 the Perfect Platonic Representation Hypothesis does not strengthen its already stated perfect-alignment claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds an interpretation linking irreversibility to erasing initialization information and presents perfect alignment as a reference point for explaining deviations. The new width-bottleneck calculation adds an applicability boundary, while a footnote discusses treating weight decay as part of entropy.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, data transformations, and pretrained-weight access information. No additional code release, hardware, timing, or reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ziyin and Chuang's Proof of a Perfect Platonic Representation Hypothesis and explicitly relates Theorem 2 to earlier symmetry-breaking dynamics. Most other bibliography differences are renumbering or updates to existing works' titles and publication details.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose expansions, introduces EDLN terminology and a descriptive title for Theorem 8, and adds explanatory footnotes and acknowledgments. It removes I from the paper title while retaining the overall section and appendix structure.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 13 are redrawn with corrected axes distinguishing models and MLP versus attention layers. Figure 5's caption changes the theoretical boundary from eta times lambda_max = 0 to 2, and Figure 1's caption identifies existing dashed markers. Figures also move with page reflow; none are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Corrected ViT axes and the Figure 5 boundary caption remove misleading labels, while Section 5.1 and Appendix B.11 clarify the interpretation and limits of perfect alignment. These provide limited overall gains despite new unresolved citation markers in Sections 1–2; the empirical coverage and central claims remain essentially unchanged.
